a.d: Used when sharing a new, private reason or circumstance that the listener is not yet aware of.
ex: 오늘은 먼저 일어나 볼게요. 내일 아침 일찍 출장이 **있거든요**. / I will get going first today. I have a business trip early tomorrow morning, you see.

b.d: Used to remind the listener of a fact they already know, refreshing common ground gently.
ex: 오늘 우리 팀 회식 있는 날**이잖아요**. 잊으셨어요? / Today is our team dinner day, you know. Did you forget?

im-c51-01.tip: Use -거든요 when giving new personal reasons; use -잖아요 only when reminding someone of something you both already know.

im-c51-01.why: Using -잖아요 for private information sounds demanding or accusatory; new information requires -거든요.

a.h: -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 (Blaming a negative factor for a bad result)
a.d: Used when holding a past or existing unfavorable condition responsible for an undesirable consequence.
ex: 어젯밤 늦게까지 게임을 **한 탓에** 오늘 하루 종일 피곤해요. / Because I played games until late last night, I am tired all day today.

b.h: -(으)ㄹ까 봐 (Taking action out of fear/concern for a risk)
b.d: Used when anticipating an undesirable possibility and proactively taking steps to prevent it.
ex: 아침에 늦잠을 **잘까 봐** 알람을 세 개나 맞춰 두었어요. / Worried that I might oversleep in the morning, I set three alarms.

im-c51-02.tip: Use -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 for actual past blunders that caused harm; use -(으)ㄹ까 봐 for future-oriented preventive actions.

im-c51-03.h: -고 해서 (Citing One of Multiple Reasons) vs -기 때문에 (Strict Singular Causality)

a.h: -고 해서 (Casually mentioning one factor among many)
a.d: Used in relaxed conversation to provide one plausible reason while subtly implying other reasons also exist.
ex: 날씨도 화창하고 **해서** 점심 먹고 호수 공원을 한 바퀴 걸었어요. / The weather was sunny and all, so after eating lunch I walked around the lake park.

b.d: Used in formal logic and written arguments to state an absolute singular cause-and-effect relationship.
ex: 날씨가 화창하**기 때문에** 공원에 사람이 많습니다. / Because the weather is sunny, there are many people in the park.

im-c51-03.tip: Pair -고 해서 with the particle -도 (A도 V고 해서) for very natural conversational phrasing.

Though small, such little moments shared with kindred spirits become a great energizer for daily life.

a.d: Used in polite conversation to provide understanding for an inevitable situation without making excuses sound aggressive.
ex: 내일 오전 회의에는 참석이 어려울 것 같습니다. 오전에 지방 출장이 **있거든요**. / It seems difficult for me to attend tomorrow morning's meeting. I have a local business trip, you see.

b.d: Used to describe an unexpected, uncontrollable external event that caused a negative mishap.
ex: 지하철이 고장 나는 **바람에** 지각을 하고 말았습니다. / Because the subway broke down, I ended up being late.

im-c51-04.tip: Use -거든요 to provide soft professional explanations; use -(으)ㄴ/는 바람에 when external accidents beyond your control caused trouble.

steps.en: Unavoidable circumstances having arisen, we ask in advance for your deep understanding.

ko: 직장 생활이나 사회생활에서 약속을 지키지 못하거나 부탁을 거절할 때는 이유를 정중하게 대는 기술이 필요합니다.
상대방을 탓하거나 '알잖아요'라며 불쑥 따지기보다는 '불가피한 사정이 생겼거든요'라며 차분하게 설명해야 합니다.

en: In workplace and social life, when unable to keep commitments or refusing requests, the skill of stating reasons politely is essential.
Rather than blaming the other person or abruptly arguing 'you know that', calmly explain saying 'unavoidable circumstances arose, you see.'
When there is your own fault, frankly admitting it and adding a heartfelt apology ensures you do not lose trust.

im-c51-04.q: What communicative approach is recommended when unable to keep a workplace commitment?
options: Calmly explaining unavoidable circumstances politely without sounding accusatory
Shouting at colleagues that they should already know
Hiding behind a pillar without saying a word
im-c51-04.why: The text advises '차분하게 설명해야 합니다... 불가피한 사정이 생겼거든요라며'.

im-c51-04.q: How can one preserve credibility when making an unintentional blunder?

Blaming the closest intern for everything
Pretending nothing ever happened
im-c51-04.why: The passage confirms '자신의 과실이 있을 때는 솔직하게 인정하고 진심 어린 사과를 덧붙여야 상대방의 신뢰를 잃지 않습니다'.
